candidates.name: Sofia History Museum
candidates.content: Museum of the history of Sofia itself, housed in the colourful old building of the Central Mineral [Water] Baths (built 1913). Exhibits include many luxurious items formerly belonging to Bulgaria's last monarchs.

candidates.name: National Museum of Military History
candidates.content: The only museum in Bulgaria with 4 types of exhibitions – open air, chronological, collections and temporary exhibitions. Over 28 000 exhibits, dated from the Antiquity to the present day. The largest open air exhibition on the Ba

candidates.name: National Museum of History
candidates.content: The National Museum of History in the Rezidentsia Boyana provide a comprehensive view on Bulgarian history from the prehistory to present, in as broad of a European context as possible. With more than 650,000 exhibits, it is one o

candidates.name: Petko R. Slaveykov Square
candidates.content: A famous square, real Sofia center with a monument of writers father and son Slaveykov. It`s a biggest open-air book market in the Balkans.There are round benches and street musicians act very often.

candidates.name: Earth and Man National Museum
candidates.content: A large mineralogical museum. In the main hall is the world's biggest collection of Giant Crystals, with dazzling jagged rocks the size of refrigerators.

candidates.name: National Institute of Archaeology and Museum
Museum of Socialist Art
candidates.content: After the Soviet Union fell and Bulgaria moved on from communism, much of the country's communist artwork was eventually collected here. Outside the museum (and free to access) is a small park crammed with statues of notable commu

candidates.name: National Art Gallery
candidates.content: Has old Bulgarian art, icons, etc. Also includes collections of the former National Gallery for Foreign Art, which are exhibited along with the 19th- and 20th-century collections of the National Art Gallery at National Gallery Squ

candidates.name: Sofia City Art Gallery
candidates.price: free entrance every second and fourth Thursday

candidates.name: St. Alexander Nevsky Cathedral
candidates.content: The largest church in the Balkans, and one of the largest Christian churches worldwide, able to hold 5,000 worshipers. Saint Alexander Nevsky was a Russian prince, and the cathedral was built to honour the Russian soldiers who die

candidates.name: St. Sophia Church
candidates.content: It was built in the 6th century, in the same wave of construction as the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople. In 1329 it gave its name to the city. It was destroyed several times and during the Ottoman rule it was used as a mosque. It

candidates.name: Boyana Church
candidates.content: This small 11th-century church and garden is on the UNESCO World Heritage List for its well-preserved murals. The layer of fresco from 1259 shows realism and emotion evocative of the early Renaissance, but painted a century earlie

candidates.name: Institute of Ethnology and Folklore Studies with Ethnographic Museum
candidates.content: Has a permanent collection of traditional Bulgarian costumes and a changing exhibition.

candidates.name: National Museum of Natural History
candidates.content: Has four floors of everything from rocks and minerals to insects and stuffed bison. It is a nice way to spend a rainy afternoon.

candidates.name: Museum of Paleontology and Historical Geology
Catholic cathedral St. Joseph
candidates.content: Holy Masses: Sa 17:30 & Su 10:30 in Bulgarian; 12:00 in Latin; 18:00 Bulgarian

candidates.name: Monument to the Unknown Soldier
candidates.content: Across from Alexander Nevsky cathedral; on the side of Hagia Sofia's Church.

candidates.name: Prince Alexander of Battenberg Square
candidates.content: The largest square in Sofia. Includes the National Art Gallery.

candidates.name: Sofia Opera and Ballet
candidates.content: During summer, open air shows in the evenings are offered.

candidates.name: Central Military Club
candidates.content: It`s a multi-purpose monument of culture building in the city center. Also known under the name Kristal.

candidates.name: National Palace of Culture
candidates.content: The biggest congress center in the Balkans (a massive monolithic communist-style building). If asking for directions, ask for NDK (en-de-ka), as most Bulgarians refer to it by this acronym.

candidates.name: Sofia Bike Tour
candidates.content: Visit Sofia and the countryside around on a "free" bike tour, every day at 11:00 and 17:00. Note, for the ride you will need to rent a bicycle with the tour operators. And like always, the word "free" is a euphemism for "tips stro

candidates.name: Playgrounds
candidates.content: If you're travelling with kids, they might love playgrounds. The "rich" one is in the park that holds Vasil Levski stadium (close to the corner with Orlov Most; there are actually two playgrounds close to this corner and you'd loo

candidates.name: Arena Cinema
candidates.content: One of the biggest Bulgarian cinema multiplex. Cinemas in Sofia play all films except children's films in their original language with Bulgarian subtitles.

candidates.name: Bar 5L
candidates.content: Speakeasy (5L is a transliteration of rooster in Bulgarian). Designer cocktails in cozy atmosphere. The key, corresponding to the day of the month, unlocks the door (not sure whether they change it at midnight).

candidates.name: Apartment
candidates.content: Popular among locals and foreigners is the "apartamenta", some sort of private club in the second floor of a turn of the 19th-century mansion where you find a series of rooms, all in different styles and wall-drawings, colourful t

candidates.name: 4km
candidates.price: Entrance is ~€10, but slightly cheaper if you arrive before midnight
candidates.content: This place plays mostly drum&bass and dubstep music.

candidates.name: The Cocktail Bar
candidates.content: Tasty cocktails, crowded in the evenings, has a summer garden (it is actually in a small park, which becomes occupied by the customers)

candidates.name: Hadjidraganovite kashti
candidates.content: Amazing restaurant just off one of Sofia's main streets. The decor is old-style Bulgarian and the food is traditional Bulgarian, plentiful and very, very tasty. Entertainment includes a Bulgarian walking band and guests are primar

candidates.name: Мекица и Кафе (Mekitsa and Coffee)
candidates.content: Here you can have brunch and the typical Bulgarian breakfast. One of them gems of Sofia. Great, hot, fresh, on the spot mekitsa. With very friendly staff. You can go to the second floor, sit at the table against the window, munch

candidates.name: Godzila
candidates.content: Godzila's first restaurant opened in 1999 in the sea capital of Bulgaria, Varna. Offers fresh salads, juicy barbecue, delicious pizza and various other dishes. Menus are in English and the staff speak English as well. There are tr

candidates.name: Veselata Gozba Restaurant
candidates.content: Good variety of main courses, soups, salads and desserts. The food is delicious. Family-operated restaurant

candidates.name: Gastrobar 6
candidates.content: Favorite place for delicious food in a great pleasant atmosphere. You feel at home

candidates.name: Ali Baba
candidates.content: Good place for a quick bit of kebabs and falafel.

candidates.name: Dream House
candidates.content: Very good vegetarian restaurant. Quick service, simple and good food, good value for money.

candidates.name: DARO
candidates.content: A breakfast restaurant

candidates.name: Pod Lipite
candidates.content: Very good traditional food. Reservation is required.

candidates.name: Motto
candidates.content: This place is always fairly busy with a trendy crowd. The decor is modern and cool, and the people typically good looking. The service is usually good, and many of the staff speak English. The food is consistent and enjoyable.

candidates.name: Pizza Victoria
candidates.content: One of the best Bulgarian pizzas.

candidates.name: Central Sofia Market Hall
candidates.content: Has many stalls selling all kinds of food, drink and cosmetics. The second floor has various fast-food cafés. As of early 2023 closed for renovations..
